title: Three Capitals in One Country: Chișinău, Tiraspol and Comrat
subRegion: Chișinău, Transnistria (de facto), and the Gagauz autonomy

bestPeriod.window: early September, warm, the wine harvest starting, and Chișinău's National Wine Day in the first weekend of October just beyond it
bestPeriod.avoid: July-August (35 °C in a city of concrete), and January-February (grey, −10 °C, nothing outdoors works)

transport.note: €35, €70 (city trolleybuses, three intercity rutieră returns, airport transfers)

gatewayAirport: Chișinău International (KIV), 13 km and 20-30 minutes from the centre. **No published airport taxi tariff and meters are unreliable**, order a **Bolt** or **Yandex Go** and take the fixed quote (roughly 160 MDL / ~€8). **Trolleybus 30** runs into town for **7 MDL** (~€0.35).
currency: Moldovan leu (MDL); Transnistria uses the unrecognised Transnistrian rouble (PRB)

hook: Chișinău is a low green city of chestnut trees and heavy Soviet concrete where the wine bars are better than the buildings and dinner for two costs €20. From it you can reach two other capitals in under two hours: Tiraspol, seat of an internationally unrecognised de facto entity with its own money, and Comrat, capital of a Turkic-speaking Orthodox autonomy inside Moldova. One week, three self-images of the same small country.

snapshot.Start / End: Chișinău → Chișinău (single base, three day trips)
snapshot.Getting there: Chișinău International (KIV), 13 km and 20-30 minutes from the centre. **No published airport taxi tariff and meters are unreliable**, order a **Bolt** or **Yandex Go** and take the fixed quote (roughly 160 MDL / ~€8). **Trolleybus 30** runs into town for **7 MDL** (~€0.35).

itinerary.title: The boulevard
itinerary.morning: Land at KIV, drop bags, and start at **Grădina Publică Ștefan cel Mare și Sfânt**, the 1818 park with the **Aleea Clasicilor**, a double row of busts of Romanian and Moldovan writers under lime trees.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk **Bulevardul Ștefan cel Mare** east: the **Nativity Cathedral** and its detached bell tower, the **Triumphal Arch**, the Government building, and the Presidency. It is one straight kilometre and it contains most of what the city puts on postcards.
itinerary.evening: **Carpe Diem** on Strada Bulgară for the first orientation in Moldovan wine, Fetească Neagră, Rara Neagră, Fetească Albă, with a knowledgeable list and by-the-glass flights.

itinerary.title: Museums and the concrete city
itinerary.morning: The **National Museum of Ethnography and Natural History** on Strada Mihail Kogălniceanu, for the **Deinotherium** skeleton, a near-complete giant prehistoric proboscidean excavated in southern Moldova, the museum's and the country's single most famous object.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Pushkin Museum** in the small house where the exiled poet lodged in 1820-23, then north to Râșcani for the **State Circus** and the **Romanița tower**, the two buildings that explain late-Soviet Chișinău better than any museum.
itinerary.evening: **Valea Morilor** lake and park at sunset, then back to **Invino** on Strada Vlaicu Pârcălab, the city's most serious wine list.

itinerary.title: Tiraspol and Transnistria
itinerary.morning: Rutieră from **Gara Centrală**. Transnistria, officially the Pridnestrovian Moldavian Republic, is an **internationally unrecognised de facto entity**: no state recognises it, Moldova claims it, and it has functioned with its own administration since 1992. At the crossing you fill in a **free migration slip** giving your name, passport number and where you are going; keep it, you surrender it on the way out. Slips are commonly issued for **up to 24 hours**; a longer stay must be registered at the migration office. **Do not photograph the checkpoint, the peacekeeping posts or any military site.**
itinerary.afternoon: In **Tiraspol**: the **House of Soviets** with its Lenin bust on 25 October Street, the war memorial and tank, and the **Kvint** distillery, brandy since 1897, the entity's best-known export, with tours and a shop. The **Sheriff Sports Complex** on the edge of town, stadium, academy and hypermarket, is the other half of the local economy.
itinerary.evening: Twenty minutes back west, **Bendery (Tighina) fortress** on the Dniester, an Ottoman rebuild of the 1530s, is the best actual monument on this side of the river. Return to Chișinău the same evening, the last rutiere run into the early evening, so check the return time before you settle in for lunch.

itinerary.title: Comrat and Gagauzia
itinerary.morning: Rutieră from **Gara de Sud** south across open steppe to **Comrat**, capital of **Găgăuzia**, an autonomous territorial unit within Moldova whose people are **Turkic-speaking Orthodox Christians**, a combination that exists almost nowhere else.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Gagauz National History and Ethnography Museum**, the **Cathedral of St John the Baptist**, the Assembly building and Comrat State University, where Gagauz is taught alongside Russian and Romanian.
itinerary.evening: Eat before you leave: **gözleme**, **kıvırma** (a coiled layered pie), **sarma**, lamb *kaurma*, and the heavy red house wine that every Gagauz household makes. Back in Chișinău by nine.

itinerary.title: Market day and the underground cellars
itinerary.morning: **Piața Centrală**, the central market: whole aisles of tomatoes, brânză sheep's cheese, dried fruit, sunflower seeds, walnuts, and a flower market that runs all year. Go before 10:00 and bring small notes.
itinerary.afternoon: **Cricova**, 15 km north, 120 km of limestone galleries entered **by vehicle**, driven through streets named after wines. Reservation is mandatory; the entry-level **Matinal** tour is 250 MDL and the tasting tours run from 400 MDL to 3,100 MDL per person.
itinerary.evening: **Vinăria Nouă** back in town for small-producer Moldovan bottles you will not find outside the country.

itinerary.title: The green city
itinerary.morning: The **Ciuflea Monastery** (Sfântul Teodor Tiron), the city's main working monastery, then the **Mazarache church** in the old lower town, the oldest surviving church in Chișinău, on the hill above the Bâc.
itinerary.afternoon: The **National Museum of History of Moldova** on Strada 31 August 1989, with the she-wolf statue outside, then the **National Art Museum** in the Herța house.
itinerary.evening: Dinner on **Strada 31 August 1989**, *zeamă* chicken broth, *plăcinte* pastries with cheese or pumpkin, *mămăligă* with brânză and sour cream, *sarmale*.

itinerary.title: Mileștii Mici, or the parks
itinerary.morning: **Mileștii Mici**, 20 minutes south: the largest wine cellar collection in the world by bottle count, again toured **by vehicle**, again reservation-only. The Excursie tour is 350 MDL on a weekday, more at evenings and weekends.
itinerary.afternoon: Or, if you have had enough underground: **Valea Trandafirilor** park, the Botanical Garden, and the Ethnographic Museum's outdoor section.
itinerary.evening: Last dinner, then Bolt to KIV, allow 40 minutes for the 13 km, more at rush hour.

accommodationStrategy.name: Central boulevard hotels
accommodationStrategy.description: everything in this itinerary except the day trips is within a 20-minute walk, and both bus stations are a short trolleybus ride. Ask for a rear-facing room, the boulevard is loud until midnight.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3-4 weeks ahead, longer for the first weekend of October (National Wine Day).

accommodationStrategy.name: Apartment rentals
accommodationStrategy.description: Moldova's best-value beds. A central one-bedroom runs well under a hotel double, with a kitchen for market produce and a washing machine. Confirm the floor and whether the lift works, many blocks are 1970s.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 1-2 weeks ahead; supply is good outside festival dates.

accommodationStrategy.name: Guesthouses in Butuceni / Trebujeni
accommodationStrategy.description: if you want one night out of the city, this is the one, limestone cliffs, a cave monastery, and home cooking, an hour north. Reserve entry is 20 MDL adult, 10 MDL reduced.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 2-4 weeks ahead; the village has only a few dozen beds.

logistics.connectivity: Moldova is **not** in EU roaming, buy a local SIM (Orange or Moldcell) at the airport, or check your operator's Moldova rate first. City wifi is widespread and fast. **Transnistrian mobile networks are separate**; your Moldovan SIM may roam expensively or not at all across the river.
logistics.emergency: **112** works throughout Moldova. In Transnistria the local services answer their own numbers; **your consulate has no consular access there**, most foreign ministries state plainly that they cannot provide assistance in the de facto entity. Note this before you cross, not after.
logistics.weather: Continental extremes. Summer highs above 35 °C with no sea to moderate them; winters to −15 °C with ice on the pavements. Spring and autumn are short, mild and the reason to come then.
logistics.bookingWindows: Cellar tours several days to a week (they are genuinely reservation-only). Opera and Organ Hall, 2-3 days midweek. Nothing else needs advance booking.
logistics.money: The **Moldovan leu (MDL)**; roughly 19-20 MDL to the euro. Cards work well in Chișinău. **In Transnistria the currency is the unrecognised Transnistrian rouble, foreign cards do not work, and there is no international ATM**, the economy there is cash-only for a visitor. Change a modest amount of MDL into roubles at a Tiraspol exchange booth, spend it, and change back before you leave: the rouble is worthless outside the territory. Euro and dollar notes are also exchangeable there.
logistics.transportRules: Rutiere are hailed at marked stops, paid in cash, and do not run to a printed timetable so much as to a fill rate. Confirm the last return departure from Tiraspol and Comrat before you commit to the day.
logistics.permits: Entering Transnistria requires the **free migration slip** issued at the crossing; overstaying it, or losing it, causes trouble on exit. **No photography of checkpoints, peacekeepers or military installations.** Moldova asks you to enter and leave the country through territory it controls, do not plan to exit from Transnistria into Ukraine on this itinerary.

proTips: **Go to Tiraspol early and come back the same day.** A day slip is simple, an overnight adds a registration step, and a same-day return removes every complication that makes people nervous about the trip.
**Carry small Moldovan notes.** Rutiere, market stalls and trolleybus conductors do not break a 500 MDL note, and the ATM will hand you nothing else.

**Language reality: Romanian is the state language, Russian is the second working language of daily life.** Older people and almost everyone in Tiraspol and Comrat answer more comfortably in Russian; younger Chișinău answers in Romanian and often English. *Bună ziua* and *mulțumesc* go a long way; *здравствуйте* and *спасибо* go equally far in the other two cities.
**Book the cellars, don't turn up.** Cricova and Mileștii Mici both take you through the tunnels **in a vehicle**, both require advance reservation, and walk-ins are routinely turned away.

**On safety, be accurate rather than dramatic.** Chișinău's ordinary crime risk is low and comparable with other European capitals; the real annoyances are unmetered taxis, poor street lighting and broken pavements. Transnistria is calm for visitors, and the issue is legal and consular ambiguity, not danger.

**Do Comrat on a weekday.** The museum and university are open, the market is running, and the rutiere are frequent; on Sunday the town is closed and you will have made a two-hour trip for a cathedral.

**Time your visit to the first weekend of October** if you can. National Wine Day fills Piața Marii Adunări Naționale with every producer in the country pouring at market prices, but book a bed a month out.

raw.Walkable blocks by name: **Bulevardul Ștefan cel Mare și Sfânt** is the spine, Ștefan cel Mare park to the Government building, 1.5 km, everything on it. **Strada 31 August 1989** runs parallel one block north with the Organ Hall and the quieter cafés. **Strada Bulgară** and **Strada Vlaicu Pârcălab** hold the wine bars. **Strada Alexandru cel Bun** and the streets down to **Piața Centrală** are the market quarter. **Valea Morilor** park is a 20-minute walk south-west from the boulevard and swallows an afternoon.
raw.Transit fares: There is **no tourist travel card** and no need for one. **Trolleybus 7 MDL** (~€0.35), **municipal bus 6 MDL**, paid to a conductor or at the validator; a contactless bank card works on most trolleybuses. City **rutiere** (privately run minibuses) cost a little more and are hailed and paid in cash to the driver.
raw.Intercity rutieră: **Chișinău → Tiraspol**: from **Gara Centrală** (the central bus station beside Piața Centrală), roughly hourly, 70 km, **1 h 30-2 h** including the crossing, around 50 MDL. **Chișinău → Comrat**: from **Gara de Sud**, every 30-60 minutes, 100 km, **1 h 45-2 h**, around 80 MDL. Both are cash, both are minibuses, neither takes reservations.
raw.Cultural booking timelines: The **National Opera and Ballet Theatre "Maria Bieșu"** and the **Organ Hall (Sala cu Orgă)** sell online and at the box office; a mid-week seat is usually available two or three days ahead, a Friday or Saturday premiere wants two weeks. **Cricova** and **Mileștii Mici** cellar tours are **reservation-only** and are not reliable as walk-ins, book several days out. Museums need no advance ticket.
raw.Architectural focal points: The **Nativity Cathedral** (Catedrala Nașterea Domnului, 1830s, Russian neoclassical, architect **Avraam Melnikov**) with its **detached bell tower**, the original was demolished in 1962 and rebuilt in 1997. The **Triumphal Arch** (1840, architect **Luca Zaușkevici**), facing it across the square. The **Organ Hall** (1911, the former City Bank, architect **Mihail Cekerul-Cuș**), Beaux-Arts. The **State Circus** (1981), the city's great **Soviet-modernist** set piece, a ribbed concrete crown on a hill in Râșcani, long derelict and under intermittent restoration; the exterior is the point.
raw.Romanița tower: The 1986 **Turnul Romanița** on Strada Mihail Sadoveanu, a 22-storey cylindrical residential high-rise by **Oleg Vronski**, is late-Soviet Chișinău's signature object: a concrete stem with cantilevered flats, half brutalist, half chamomile flower. Residential, so admire from the street.
